problem: Existing VLN-CE methods rely on implicit language embeddings or visual-only semantics, so waypoint prediction and topological planning lack explicit grounding in instruction-level landmarks, hurting generalization in unseen environments.
motivation: Humans navigate by landmark-referenced subgoals, and instructions contain structured landmark information that could guide both local waypoint prediction and global planning. Explicitly extracting landmarks from instructions and verifying them against visual observations should give semantic anchors that reduce ambiguity.
key_idea: Extract ordered landmarks (plus co-occurring landmarks) from instructions offline with an LLM, correct them with CLIP-based visual scoring, and fuse the resulting landmark features into both the waypoint predictor and the topological node encodings of an ETPNav-style planner.
insight: The ablation (Table 2) shows the two insertion points help differently. Landmarks in waypoint prediction mainly improve trajectory efficiency (TL down, SPL up 3 points on val-unseen over the CWP-style baseline), while landmarks in node encoding mainly raise OSR and SR (the paper reports +7 OSR, +3 SR). Using both gives the best results, so the two are complementary. Table 3 shows landmarks also make waypoints more open-space (%Open 82.87 to 84.05) and more accurate (dH 2.01 to 1.81). Note the Table 2 rows are confusing: the first row equals CWP-CMA numbers and the third equals ETPNav numbers.
method: LLM landmark extraction: DeepSeek with customized prompts and in-context examples extracts 3-8 navigation-ordered concrete landmarks per instruction and five co-occurring landmarks for each; done offline for all 16,844 R2R-CE instructions.

Vision-constrained landmark scoring: a CLIP image and text encoder picks the effective primary landmark between adjacent landmarks via a softmax over similarity, then estimates per-view observation probabilities of each landmark.

Learnable co-occurrence scoring: an embedding module (Linear, ReLU, LayerNorm, Dropout) maps instruction and observation features to a state feature, and cosine scores S_la and S_co weight the primary and co-occurring landmark features into a corrected landmark feature F_U.

Landmark-enhanced waypoint predictor: DINOv2 RGB encoder, a point-goal-pretrained ResNet-50 depth encoder and the landmark feature are pooled, layer-normed and summed, then fed to a 3-layer, 12-head Transformer with local sector attention and an MLP head that outputs a 120x12 polar heatmap.
Topological map and localization: predicted waypoints become graph nodes, and a localization function merges a waypoint into an existing node when the Euclidean distance is below a threshold γ.

Landmark-augmented cross-modal planner: BERT instruction encoder and a LXMERT-style graph encoder with Graph-Aware Self-Attention using the shortest-path distance matrix. Node embeddings include landmark-aware features, relative pose and step embeddings. It predicts a stop score per node, picks the best unvisited node as the goal, and Dijkstra gives the path.
Low-level control: executes forward 0.25 m, turn 15° and stop along the planned path.

setting.backbone: ETPNav-style planner: CLIP ViT-B/32 (frozen) RGB features, ResNet-50 depth, BERT instruction encoder and a graph Transformer, with a 3-layer waypoint Transformer; DeepSeek LLM (frozen, offline) and CLIP (frozen encoders, learnable scoring module) for landmarks
setting.training_data: R2R-CE train split, augmented with DeepSeek-generated instruction landmarks and co-occurring landmarks; initialized from a pretrained checkpoint, 20k iterations, batch size 50, scheduled sampling
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 views, 90° FoV, 256x256) plus instruction
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN 15° / STOP, with high-level topological waypoint/node selection

numbers.backbone: CLIP ViT-B/32 + ResNet-50 + BERT graph planner with DeepSeek/CLIP landmark features
numbers.extra: instruction landmarks precomputed offline by DeepSeek; pretrained-checkpoint init

results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, FILD-Nav reaches SR 59, SPL 52 and OSR 72, beating the strongest baseline ETPNav (SR 57, SPL 49, OSR 65) and MV-Topo (57.5 / 49.1 / 63). It also improves on val-seen (SR 67, SPL 61, OSR 76), with comparable NE and shorter TL.
limitations: Gains are modest (+2 SR, +3 SPL on val-unseen). Evaluation is on R2R-CE only, with no RxR-CE or real-robot tests. The test row duplicates the val-unseen numbers, and the ablation table is inconsistent with the main table and with the paper's text.

Relies on offline LLM landmark preprocessing for every instruction, which needs LLM access and may propagate hallucinated landmarks. There are no ablations of the CLIP correction module, co-occurring landmarks or the LLM choice.
No variance or seeds reported; the ablation baselines are ETPNav and CWP-CMA numbers copied from other papers.
